name: Apollo 11
description: US astronauts became the first to perform a crewed lunar landing and return to Earth.
objective: Perform crewed lunar landing

name: Hubble Space Telescope
description: Space-based observatory launched to study the universe, free from Earth's atmospheric distortion.
objective: Understand the universe

name: Mars 2020: Perseverance Rover
description: Landing Feb. 18, 2021 on Mars, Perseverance Rover collects samples of Martian rock to search for signs of ancient microbial life.
objective: Seek signs of ancient life; Collect samples of rock and regolith

name: Project Mercury
description: USA's first human spaceflight program that included 6 crewed flights piloted by 'The Mercury Seven' military test pilots. It was foundational stepping stone into space, establishing the critical engineering, global communication networks, and human physiological baselines required for further exploration.
objective: First human spaceflight program; Recover crew and spacecraft safely; Evaluate human performan in space; Orbit a crewed spaceraft

name: James Webb Space Telescope
description: Space telescope designed to study the early universe, galaxy formation, stars, and planetary systems. It orbits the Sun near Earth's second Lagrange point (L2).
objective: Study the early universe and the formation of stars and planetary systems

name: Kepler / K2
description: Space telescope that searched for planets orbiting distant stars and expanded its observations during the K2 mission. It discovered thousands of exoplanets and candidates.
objective: Search for exoplanets

name: Spitzer Space Telescope
description: Space telescope that observed the universe in infrared light, studying objects ranging from nearby planets and stars to distant galaxies. It revealed Saturn's wispy rings and the first telescope to detect light from an exoplanet, and the first known star system with seven Earth-sized exoplanets.
objective: Study the universe in infrared

name: Spirit
description: Uncovered strong evidence that Mars was once a much wetter planet, studying the history of climate and water in places where conditions may have once been favorable to life. Travelled 5 miles and operated for 6 years, more than 25 times its original intended lifetime.
objective: Investigate evidence of past water on Mars; Mars surface exploration

name: Voyager 1
description: The farthest spacecraft from Earth, Voyager 1 flew by Jupiter and Saturn making discoveries of new moons and Saturns new ring before crossing into interstellar space in August 2012. It continues to return data on the interstellar environment on an extended mission to reach one light-day away from Earth, more than 49 years in mission.
objective: Explore Jupiter and Saturn; Study the outer solar system; Investigate interstellar space

name: Voyager 2
description: The only spacecraft to visit all four giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune at close range. It entered interstellar space - the second to do so after Voyager 1 - in December 2018 and continues to study the boundary of the Sun's influence.
target: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Interstellar Space
objective: Explore the giant planets; Study the heliosphere and interstellar space

name: Cassini-Huygens
description: A NASA-ESA-Italian Space Agency mission that orbited Saturn for 13 years and delivered the Huygens probe to the moon Titan. It revealed Enceladus's global ocean and hydrothermal activity, Titan's methane seas, and detailed structure of Saturn's rings.
objective: Study Saturn, its rings, moons, and magnetosphere; Land the Huygens probe on Titan

name: New Horizons
description: The first spacecraft to explore Pluto up close, flying by the dwarf planet and its moons on July 14, 2015. It later flew by Arrokoth - becoming the most distant object explored upclose, in the Kuiper Belt - massive, ring-shaped region of icy objects and dwarf planets just beyond Neptune - on January 1, 2019, and continues studying the Kuiper Belt.
target: Outer edge of solar system, Pluto, Kuiper Belt
objective: Perform the first close exploration of Pluto and its moons; Study Kuiper Belt objects

name: Mars Science Laboratory: Curiosity Rover
description: Part of the Mars Science Laboratory mission, Curiosity landed in Gale Crater on August 6, 2012. It investigates whether Mars ever had conditions capable of supporting microbial life and analyzes Martian rock, soil, and atmosphere.
objective: Determine if Mars was ever able to support microbial life; Study Martian geology and climate

name: Opportunity Rover
description: Twin rover to Spirit, Opportunity landed in Meridiani Planum in January 2004 and found mineral evidence that Mars once had liquid water. It operated for nearly 15 years, far exceeding its planned 90-day mission. Opportunity ran for 28 miles before falling silent.
objective: Investigate evidence of past water on Mars; Explore Martian geology

name: Juno
description: Juno entered orbit around Jupiter on July 4, 2016, becoming the first spacecraft to peer beneath Jupiter's dense clouds. It aims to understand the planet's origin and evolution. It maps the magentic and gravitational fields. It studies the atmosphere, magnetosphere, and structures.
objective: Explore the Jovian system

name: OSIRIS-REx
description: The first U.S. mission to collect a sample from a near-Earth asteroid. OSIRIS-REx rendezvoused with asteroid Bennu, collected rock and dust in 2020, and returned the sample capsule to Earth in September 2023. Scientists hope to reveal whether asteroids that collided with Earth billions of years ago, delivered water and other ingredients for life on Earth
objective: Collect and return a sample of asteroid Bennu, Study the origins of the solar system

name: Parker Solar Probe
description: The first spacecraft to fly through the Sun's corona, its upper atmosphere, in 2021. Parker studies the solar wind, coronal heating, and energetic particles while orbiting closer to the Sun than any prior spacecraft.
objective: Study the Sun's corona and solar wind; Trace how energy and heat move through the solar atmosphere

name: Artemis I
description: The first flight test of NASA's Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft. The uncrewed mission traveled around the Moon and back to Earth, demonstrating systems needed for future crewed lunar exploration and beyond.
objective: Test SLS and Orion for deep-space human exploration; Demonstrate capability to return to the Moon

name: Galileo
description: The first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter, Galileo studied the planet, its major moons, rings, and magnetosphere. It delivered a probe into Jupiter's atmosphere, found evidence supporting a subsurface ocean on Europa, and discovered that Ganymede generates its own magnetic field. After completing its primary mission, it was extended three times before ending with a deliberate plunge into Jupiter to prevent possible contamination of Jupiter's moon Europa by accidental collision.
objective: Study Jupiter's atmosphere and magnetosphere; Investigate its moons and rings; Measure the atmosphere directly with an entry probe

name: Magellan
description: Magellan used synthetic aperture radar to map approximately 98 percent of Venus's surface through its thick clouds - the first to do so and the first space probe launched by a space shuttle: Atlantis. Its observations revealed extensive volcanic terrain and helped scientists investigate the planet's geology and gravity. The mission ended after the spacecraft was directed into the Venusian atmosphere.
objective: Image the entire surface of Venus; Study surface geology and Venus' gravity field

name: MESSENGER
description: Short for MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging, it was the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury. MESSENGER mapped the planet and investigated its composition, geological history, magnetic field, and tenuous exosphere. It confirmed that deposits in permanently shadowed polar regions are predominantly water ice. After exhausting its propellant, the spacecraft impacted Mercury's surface.
objective: Mercury mapping and discoveries; Study Mercury's geology, magnetic field, and chemical composition

name: Dawn
description: Dawn explored the giant asteroid Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres in the main asteroid belt, becoming the first spacecraft to orbit two separate destinations beyond Earth as NASA's first truly interplanetary spaceship. Using ion propulsion to travel between the two worlds, it studied their contrasting geology and provided evidence about the early history of the solar system. The mission ended after the spacecraft exhausted its hydrazine fuel.
objective: Study and compare Vesta and Ceres; Study early solar system evolution

name: InSight
description: InSight landed in Elysium Planitia on November 26, 2018, to investigate the deep interior of Mars. Its seismic observations helped scientists study marsquakes and the structure of the planet's crust, mantle, and core. The solar-powered lander eventually lost power as dust accumulated on its solar panels.
objective: Study Mars' interior structure

name: Mars Pathfinder
description: Mars Pathfinder landed in Ares Vallis on July 4, 1997, demonstrating an airbag-cushioned landing system and delivering Sojourner, the first rover to operate on Mars. The lander and its rover Sojourner examined rocks, soil, and atmospheric conditions, returning observations consistent with a warmer and wetter Martian past.
objective: Land a rover on Mars

name: Viking 1
description: Viking 1 combined an orbiter with a lander that touched down in Chryse Planitia on July 20, 1976, becoming the first spacecraft to conduct a sustained, successful mission on the Martian surface. It photographed the landscape, measured weather, analyzed soil, and performed experiments searching for evidence of life. Its orbiter ended operations in 1980, while the lander continued until 1982.
objective: Map Mars from orbit; Study surface composition and weather; Search for evidence of microbial life

name: Viking 2
description: Viking 2 paired an orbiter with a lander that touched down in Utopia Planitia on September 3, 1976. It studied Martian surface materials, monitored weather, photographed its surroundings, and conducted biological experiments. The orbiter ceased operations in 1978, while the lander continued transmitting until 1980.
objective: Image Mars and its moons; Investigate surface materials and atmospheric conditions; Search for evidence of microbial life

name: Apollo 13
description: Apollo 13 was intended to land astronauts in the Moon's Fra Mauro region, but an oxygen tank failure forced the crew to abandon the landing. Astronauts Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise used the lunar module as a lifeboat during the return journey and splashed down safely on Earth.
objective: Attempt a crewed landing in the Fra Mauro region; Following spacecraft emergency, return crew safely to Earth

name: Apollo 12
description: The second crewed mission to land astronauts on the Moon, Apollo 12 demonstrated a precise landing near the Surveyor 3 spacecraft. The crew collected lunar samples and brought back parts of Surveyor 3 to help scientists study how equipment holds up on the lunar surface.
objective: Perform a crewed lunar landing; Collect lunar samples; Study the lunar surface

name: Apollo 14
description: Apollo 14 was the third crewed mission to land astronauts on the Moon, touching down in the Fra Mauro region. The crew collected lunar rocks and soil to investigate the Moon's geological history and conducted experiments on the surface.
objective: Perform a crewed lunar landing; Collect lunar samples; Investigate lunar geology

name: Apollo 15
description: Apollo 15 was the first Apollo mission to use a lunar rover, allowing astronauts to explore farther from their landing site. The crew studied the Moon's Hadley-Apennine region, collecting samples and investigating its mountains, craters, and ancient volcanic history.
objective: Explore the lunar surface by rover; Collect lunar samples; Study lunar geology

name: Apollo 16
description: Apollo 16 was the fifth crewed mission to land astronauts on the Moon and the first to explore the lunar highlands. The crew used a lunar rover to investigate the region, collect rock samples, and study how the Moon's surface formed and changed over time.
objective: Explore the lunar highlands; Collect lunar samples; Investigate the Moon's geological history

name: Mars Odyssey
description: Mars Odyssey is an orbiter that mapped the chemical elements and minerals across the Martian surface, helping scientists identify evidence of water ice beneath the ground. It continues to study Mars and relay data from surface missions back to Earth.
objective: Map Martian surface composition; Locate water ice; Support communications with Mars landers and rovers

name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
description: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter studies the surface and atmosphere of Mars using high-resolution cameras and other scientific instruments. Its observations help scientists investigate the planet's history of water and identify potential landing sites for future missions.
objective: Search for evidence of past water; Map Martian surface features; Identify landing sites; Relay data from surface missions

name: MAVEN
description: MAVEN studied the upper atmosphere of Mars to understand how the planet lost much of its atmosphere over time. Its observations helped scientists investigate how solar wind and other processes have shaped Mars's climate and habitability.
objective: Study the Martian upper atmosphere; Investigate atmospheric loss; Understand Mars's climate history

name: Mars Global Surveyor
description: Mars Global Surveyor orbited Mars for nearly a decade, mapping its surface and studying its atmosphere, magnetic field, and gravity. Its observations revealed evidence of ancient water-related features and helped guide later Mars exploration missions.
objective: Map the Martian surface; Study the atmosphere and magnetic field; Investigate evidence of past water

name: Pioneer 10
description: Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to fly past Jupiter and the first NASA mission sent to explore the outer planets. It studied Jupiter's atmosphere and magnetic environment before continuing outward on a trajectory away from the solar system.
objective: Perform the first Jupiter flyby; Study Jupiter's atmosphere and magnetic field; Explore the outer solar system

name: Pioneer 11
description: Pioneer 11 followed Pioneer 10 to Jupiter before continuing to Saturn, becoming the first spacecraft to fly past Saturn. Its observations provided close-up measurements of both planets and helped prepare scientists for later missions to the outer solar system.
objective: Explore Jupiter and Saturn; Study planetary atmospheres and magnetic fields; Investigate Saturn's rings

name: Stardust / Stardust NExT
description: Stardust collected dust from comet Wild 2 and returned the samples to Earth, becoming the first mission to bring comet material back for laboratory study. Its extended mission later flew past another comet, giving scientists a closer look at how these icy objects change over time.
objective: Collect comet dust; Return samples to Earth; Study comets up close

name: NEAR Shoemaker
description: NEAR Shoemaker was the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid, studying Eros's shape, surface, composition, and geology. After completing its orbital mission, it successfully touched down on the asteroid, returning additional data from the surface.
objective: Orbit and study asteroid Eros; Map its surface and composition; Investigate asteroid structure

name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
description: The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter maps the Moon's surface in detail, studying its terrain, temperature, and radiation environment. Its observations help scientists understand lunar resources and identify locations that may be useful for future crewed exploration.
objective: Map the lunar surface; Study potential water ice and resources; Identify landing sites for future missions

name: Phoenix Mars Lander
description: Phoenix landed in the Martian arctic and used a robotic arm to dig into the soil, finding water ice beneath the surface. The mission studied the soil and local weather to understand whether the environment could have supported conditions favorable to life.
objective: Search for water ice; Analyze Martian soil; Study the polar environment

name: Deep Impact
description: Deep Impact sent an impactor into comet Tempel 1 to expose material beneath its surface and study the comet's composition. Its extended mission later observed another comet, helping scientists compare these icy bodies and learn more about the early solar system.
objective: Impact and study a comet; Analyze material beneath the surface; Compare comet structures

name: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)
description: SOHO is a space observatory that studies the Sun's interior, atmosphere, and outward flow of solar wind. Its long-running observations have helped scientists understand solar activity and improve monitoring of events that can affect Earth.
objective: Study the Sun's interior and atmosphere; Observe solar wind; Monitor solar activity

name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
description: Chandra is a space telescope designed to observe X-rays from extremely hot and energetic regions of the universe. It studies objects such as black holes, exploding stars, and galaxy clusters, revealing details that are difficult to detect using visible light alone.
objective: Observe the universe in X-rays; Study black holes and exploding stars; Investigate galaxy clusters
